title: Wire the herdr executor into dispatch, and put the substrate in provenance
description:
Wire the herdr executor into dispatch, and put the substrate in provenance.
These are the epic's two NOT MET acceptance items, found by the final review.

## 1. The executor is unreachable, not merely unexercised

- internal/reconcile/dispatch.go:1390 unconditionally builds subprocess.New.
- internal/reconcile/profiles.go:311 actively REFUSES any profile naming a
  non-subprocess executor: "profile %s names executor %q and this phase has
  one".
- There is no --executor flag.

So the epic's headline acceptance — an operator runs a real ticks epic through
`ticfac run-epic` on Herdr — cannot be attempted. Everything the executor builds
is latent.

Do:
- Select the executor from the resolved profile rather than hardcoding one, and
  lift usableProfile's refusal to admit herdr now that this phase has two. Keep
  the refusal's PURPOSE intact: a profile naming an executor the run did not use
  is provenance that lies, so the check becomes "can this build honour it",
  not "is it the only one".
- Land ticks 1eq and etp FIRST or alongside. They are the defects a first real
  run hits, and both are in the paths this tick makes reachable.
- Then run a real epic through it, end to end, and show the run. That is the
  acceptance, not a test.

## 2. The substrate is not in provenance

runstate.Provenance (internal/runstate/records.go:28-50) has no herdr protocol
or server version field, and it is a CLOSED object whose decoder rejects unknown
properties. The values live only on herdr's private attemptRecord
(internal/exec/herdr/store.go:97-101), so a run that spans a herdr upgrade
cannot be diagnosed from the durable record.

This contradicts the epic description and the 2026-09-11 split decision, both of
which put the substrate in provenance. It needs the same upstream bundle bump
that tick 9t0 carried for the tier and the findings channel — read that tick's
RESULT for the pattern.

Also fix, from the same review: internal/exec/herdr/doc.go:93 claims more than
its test asserts about this.
acceptance_criteria: run-epic dispatches through the executor its resolved profile names, with usableProfile admitting herdr while still refusing an executor this build cannot honour; a real ticks epic completes end to end through ticfac run-epic on herdr and the run is shown, not described; the herdr protocol and server version are fields of the pinned Provenance object rather than a private record, landed through the contract bundle the way 9t0 landed the tier and the findings channel; doc.go no longer claims more than its test asserts; make test-short green.
